titleEn: New FCC proposal could ‘retroactively ban’ some existing ag spray drones, warns DJI
titleZh: FCC新提案或“追溯性禁止”部分现有农用喷雾无人机，DJI发出警告
summaryZh: 美国联邦通信委员会（FCC）于2025年12月22日禁止销售外国制造无人机后，又于2026年7月21日提出新提案，拟禁止销售已获授权的“军用级”外国无人机，其定义宽泛，可能涵盖农业喷雾无人机。DJI警告称，这将构成“追溯性禁令”，影响美国农民和公共安全机构，增加成本、限制选择，并让美国在技术上落后于其他国家。目前该提案正在公开征求意见，截止日期为9月2日。
featuredReason: 该新闻直接影响美国农业无人机市场，对依赖先进植保技术的智慧畜牧和种植业者具有重大政策风险提示，值得关注其后续进展并评估替代方案。
contentFull:
New proposals from the US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) cracking down on foreign-made “military grade” drones could “amount to a ban on future sales of certified and currently available products” widely used to spray crops, claims ag spray drone market leader DJI.

The Chinese firm is already wrestling with the FCC’s bombshell Dec 22, 2025 ruling to block the sale of new foreign-made models and critical components, which has upended a sector dominated by overseas vendors.

However, a July 21 public notice seeks comment on proposals to ban sales of current models of foreign-made “military-grade” UAS products on the FCC’s covered list of comms equipment and services “deemed to pose an unacceptable risk” to national security.

This means that selected products “already cleared for the US market could no longer be imported or sold, while covered replacement components could also become harder, or impossible, to obtain,” claims DJI.

“People could continue using DJI products they already own, but the same models in use today might no longer be available to purchase in the future. This is a total reversal from the FCC’s previous position, and it is US operators that would bear the cost.”

‘Economic poison’

The proposal—up for public comment until September 2—is framed as targeting “military-grade” drones. However, the FCC’s definition includes previously-authorized foreign-made drones with thermal imaging, LiDAR sensing, swarming drones, drone docking stations, drones weighing 55lbs+ on takeoff, and aerosol drones capable of dispensing “economic poison.”

The latter is defined as “any substance intended for preventing, destroying, repelling, or mitigating pests (insects, rodents, nematodes, fungi, weeds), viruses, or intended for use as a plant defoliant, or drying agent.”

This, claims DJI, “is a roundabout way of describing every agricultural drone that can spray pesticides or spread seeds. American farmers would be crippled if they can no longer treat their crops with technology that’s proven to save water, increase yields, and lower operational costs.”

It adds: “This could affect DJI FlyCart and agricultural drones, enterprise platforms, and dock stations  – even though these are civilian and commercial tools, not military-grade equipment. Restricting products already cleared for sale would increase costs, limit choice, and put essential technology further out of reach for the Americans who rely on it.”

A ‘retroactive ban’ on some previously authorized drones

While DJI does not design or manufacture military-grade equipment, the FCC’s proposed definition is “broad enough to capture many of the civilian drones Americans rely on every day,” claims DJI.

According to DJI, “The way the FCC has set up the proposal directly targets—and would retroactively ban—drones that are widely used by American farmers and public safety agencies.”

According to the Drone Advocacy Alliance, a group sponsored by DJI, “This is a total reversal from the FCC who previously stated that approved devices would continue to be marketed and sold and that firmware and software updates could continue normally.

“Meanwhile, other countries across the globe—including our neighbors Canada and Mexico—will continue to have access to these products alongside the latest and greatest technology, putting us at a disadvantage.”

Exemptions

Since blocking new authorizations for foreign-made drones in December, the FCC has granted a series of exemptions, including to several non-Chinese drone makers following national-security reviews by the Department of War.

According to the FCC’s July 21 document, the proposed ban on foreign-made military drones would not apply to foreign-made drones and critical components that are exempt from the FCC’s covered list. These include products on the Defense Contract Management Agency’s Blue UAS Cleared List, products that qualify as “domestic end products” under the Buy American Standard, and products granted conditional approval by the Department of War or Department of Homeland Security.

Finally, the proposed ban would not apply to products for federal government use or imports for commercial testing and product development. Existing owners can also continue operating previously purchased affected drones.

translationZh:
美国联邦通信委员会（FCC）针对外国制造的“军用级”无人机提出的新提案，可能“相当于禁止销售已认证且目前可用的产品”，农业喷雾无人机市场领导者DJI声称，这些产品广泛用于作物喷洒。

这家中国公司已经在应对FCC于2025年12月22日发布的重磅裁决，该裁决禁止销售新的外国制造型号和关键组件，这颠覆了一个由海外供应商主导的行业。

然而，7月21日的一份公开通知征求对一项提案的意见，该提案旨在禁止销售FCC受保护清单上所列的外国制造“军用级”无人机产品，这些通信设备和服务被认定“对美国国家安全构成不可接受的风险”。

这意味着，部分“已经获准进入美国市场的产品可能不再被进口或销售，而受保护的关键替换组件也可能变得更难或无法获得，”DJI声称。

“人们可以继续使用他们已经拥有的DJI产品，但今天在使用的相同型号未来可能无法购买。这与FCC之前的立场完全相反，而美国运营商将承担这一代价。”

**‘经济毒药’**

该提案——公开征求意见截止日期为9月2日——被定位为针对“军用级”无人机。然而，FCC的定义包括先前已获授权的外国制造无人机，这些无人机具备热成像、激光雷达传感、蜂群无人机、无人机对接站、起飞重量超过55磅的无人机，以及能够喷洒“经济毒药”的气溶胶无人机。

后者被定义为“任何旨在预防、破坏、驱除或减轻害虫（昆虫、啮齿动物、线虫、真菌、杂草）、病毒，或用作植物落叶剂或干燥剂的物质。”

DJI声称，这“是一种迂回的方式来描述每一架可以喷洒农药或播撒种子的农业无人机。如果美国农民无法再使用这种已被证明能节约用水、提高产量并降低运营成本的技术来治疗他们的作物，他们将会受到重创。”

它补充道：“这可能会影响DJI FlyCart和农业无人机、企业平台和对接站——尽管这些是民用和商业工具，而非军用级设备。限制已经获准销售的产品将增加成本、限制选择，并使美国依赖者更难获得关键技术。”

**对部分先前已授权无人机的‘追溯性禁令’**

虽然DJI不设计或制造军用级设备，但FCC的拟议定义“足够宽泛，可以涵盖美国人日常依赖的许多民用无人机，”DJI声称。

据DJI称，“FCC设置提案的方式直接针对——并将追溯性地禁止——美国农民和公共安全机构广泛使用的无人机。”

根据DJI赞助的无人机倡导联盟的说法，“这是FCC的完全逆转，此前FCC表示已批准的设备将继续销售和营销，固件和软件更新可以正常继续。

“与此同时，全球其他国家——包括我们的邻国加拿大和墨西哥——将继续获得这些产品以及最新技术，使我们处于劣势。”

**豁免**

自12月禁止外国制造无人机的新授权以来，FCC已授予一系列豁免，包括在战争部进行国家安全审查后授予几家非中国无人机制造商的豁免。

根据FCC 7月21日的文件，拟议的外国制造军用无人机禁令不适用于不受FCC受保护清单约束的外国制造无人机和关键组件。这些包括国防合同管理署的“蓝色无人机清关清单”上的产品，符合《购买美国货标准》中“国内最终产品”资格的产品，以及获得战争部或国土安全部有条件批准的产品。

最后，拟议的禁令不适用于联邦政府使用的产品或用于商业测试和产品开发的进口产品。现有所有者也可以继续操作先前购买的受影响无人机。
author: Elaine Watson
